question: In Volume-Controlled Ventilation (VCV), which parameter remains FIXED and which is allowed to vary?

answers.text: Fixed: peak inspiratory pressure; Variable: tidal volume

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes Pressure-Controlled Ventilation (PCV), not VCV. In PCV the set pressure is fixed and the resulting tidal volume varies with lung compliance.

answers.text: Fixed: tidal volume; Variable: peak inspiratory pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In VCV a pre-set tidal volume is delivered on every breath; the resulting airway pressure varies according to the patient's lung compliance and resistance — a rising pressure signals worsening compliance.

answers.text: Fixed: respiratory rate; Variable: tidal volume and pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Respiratory rate is set in both VCV and PCV, but it is not the defining differentiating parameter between modes.
FiO2 and PEEP are set parameters in all modes but do not define the VCV/PCV distinction.

overallFeedback.feedback: In VCV: set tidal volume delivered → pressure varies. In PCV: set pressure applied → tidal volume varies. The defining feature is what is fixed — volume (VCV) or pressure (PCV).
Well done. Understanding VCV vs PCV is essential for recognising ventilator alarms — a high-pressure alarm in VCV signals reduced compliance or obstruction.
